short: Design tokens, base styles and the contrast gate
is: The two global stylesheets the root layout imports once (tokens.css, base.css), and the contrast gate: a declared list of the dark theme's colour pairs that a node spec checks against WCAG 2.2 AA on every gate.
conventions: Components name a semantic `--color-*` token, never a palette step; a control's identifying edge (text box, checkbox, secondary or form button, toggle track) uses `--color-control-edge`, and `--color-border` stays for decoration.

Every token painted as a text, icon, edge, outline, fill, stroke or ring colour has a pair in `contrast-pairs.ts` (or a commented entry in its decorative list); a `background` names only a declared background token or a named filled part; `--color-*` and `--palette-*` tokens are defined only in `tokens.css`. The contrast spec fails on each.

A greyed value (an unticked checkbox's value) is painted `--color-text-muted`, never lowered with `opacity`: the guard cannot see opacity or which background a component sits on, so a dialog's colours are paired on `--color-surface` by name.
The pairs cover the dark theme only — every top-level `:root` block of `tokens.css`, a later one winning — the theme 0.1 ships; light and the `prefers-contrast: more` overrides are not checked.
A failing pair is fixed in the token, not in the test: the palette is a placeholder until the design sync.

fs.name: base.css
fs.role: element defaults, text-box and form-button edges, the focus ring, .visually-hidden, the one 48rem phone breakpoint behind .desktop-only/.phone-only, --shell-columns and the full-screen dialog's --full-dialog-* switches

fs.name: contrast-pairs.ts
fs.role: the declared pairs (foreground token, the backgrounds it sits on, text | largeText | nonText, where it is used), the thresholds per kind, the closed list of background tokens, the filled parts (toggle thumbs), and the decorative-token list

fs.name: contrast.spec.ts
fs.role: node spec: the arithmetic against known values, one test per declared pair at its threshold, and the completeness guard (every painted token paired, every fill a declared background, no token defined outside tokens.css)

fs.name: contrast.ts
fs.role: contrast arithmetic: reads the dark theme's top-level :root blocks (later wins), follows var() chains, parses hex and rgb() colours, composites a translucent colour, and computes relative luminance and the contrast ratio

fs.name: tokens.css
fs.role: palette → semantic → layout custom properties; dark on :root, light under [data-theme='light'], reduced-motion and more-contrast overrides

notes: Why the edge token points at `--color-text-muted` rather than a palette step: the light theme stays untouched yet still gets an edge that follows its own muted text; under `prefers-contrast: more` the edge brightens with it.
The decorative list is per token, so a decorative token reused as a control edge escapes the guard; the convention above (control edges use `--color-control-edge`) is what keeps that from happening.

The guard does not see palette steps or literal colours named outside tokens.css, paint properties outside its lists (`-webkit-text-fill-color`, `background-image`), or `opacity` lowering a painted colour; none is used today (the one `opacity`, a busy button, is an inactive control).
